name: Altgutnisch

catalog_locator: §57 'Phonetische übersicht', pp. 49-50 (pp. 73-74 of archive.org altschwedischegr00noreuoft); secondary stress §57.II pp. 50-53; Old Gutnish scope §8 p. 17, §9 pp. 22-23. Noreen 1913 §54 p. 90.
catalog_quote: § 57. Über die aschw. (exspiratorische) betonung ist bis jetzt folgendes ermittelt worden [...] Eine silbe kann entweder haupttonig, stark nebentonig, schwach nebentonig oder endlich unbetont (mit 'unton' versehen) sein. [...] I. Der hauptton ruht der regel nach: A) In zusammengesetzten wörtern auf der wurzelsilbe des ersten gliedes. Jedoch gibt es sehr viele wörter mit einsilbigem erstem gliede, bei denen die wurzelsilbe des letzten gliedes den hauptton trägt. Solche sind: 1. Eine ganze menge von zusammensetzungen, deren erstes glied ein präfix oder eine partikel ist, und zwar besonders: a) Alle mit den präfixen be- 'be-', of- 'allzu' und æm- 'ebenso', die meisten mit for- 'ver-' (aber nicht mit for- 'vor-') sowie viele mit and- 'gegen', mis- 'miss-', ō- (ū-) 'un-' und unt- 'ent-' zusammengesetzte wörter [...] b) Viele mit den partikeln ā 'an', af 'ab', at 'bei', bort 'weg', fram 'hervor', in 'hinein', til 'hinzu', um 'um', up 'hinauf', ūt 'hinaus' und væl 'wol' zusammengesetzte, besonders verben [...] B) In einfachen wörtern auf der wurzelsilbe. Jedoch ist in vielen fällen die ableitungssilbe haupttonig, nämlich: 1. Alle lehnwörter auf -era, -inna und -issa haben haupttonige pænultima, diejenigen auf -eri und -ær haupttonige ultima, z. b. hantéra hantieren, kesarínna kaiserin, abbadíssa äbtissin; fiskerí fischerei, konstenǣr künstler.

new_statements.translation: §57. On Old Swedish (expiratory) stress the following has so far been established [...] A syllable can be main-stressed, strongly secondary-stressed, weakly secondary-stressed or unstressed. [...] I. The main stress rests as a rule: A) in compound words on the root syllable of the first member; however there are very many words with a monosyllabic first member in which the root syllable of the last member bears the main stress [...] B) in simple words on the root syllable; however in many cases the derivational syllable is main-stressed, namely: 1. all loanwords in -era, -inna, -issa have main-stressed penult, those in -eri and -ær main-stressed ultima.
new_statements.citation: Noreen, Adolf. 1904. Altschwedische Grammatik mit Einschluss des Altgutnischen. Halle: Max Niemeyer.
new_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File check: (43 MB, archive.org Toronto scan) and its scanned text are present with. At the scanned textand p. 73 (book p. 49, running head '§ 57. Phonetische übersicht. 49') I find: '§ 57. Über die asehw. (exspiratorisehe) betonung ist bis jetzt folgendes ennittelt worden.. Eine silbe kann entweder haupttonig, stark nebentonig, schwach nebentonig oder endlich unbetont (mit "unton" versehen) sein.. I. Der hauptton ruht der regel nach: A) In zusammengesetzten Wörtern auf der Wurzelsilbe des ersten gliedes. Jedoch gibt es sehr viele Wörter mit einsilbigem erstem gliede. bei denen die Wurzelsilbe des letzten gliedes den hauptton trägt.' and on book p. 50: 'B) In einfachen Wörtern auf der Wurze…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Main (expiratory) stress falls on the root syllable of simplex words (in practice the first syllable of native words) and on the root syllable of the first member of compounds; certain prefixes/particles (be-, of-, æm-, most for-, many and-, mis-, o-, unt-, and particle verbs like afinna) leave main stress on the second member, and some loan suffixes (-era, -inna, -issa, -eri, -ær) and alternately -ing/-ung attract main stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: §57.II (pp. 50-53): strong secondary stress on the root syllable of the non-main-stressed compound member (suffixed article always weak), and on certain long derivational/inflectional syllables depending on the quantity of the root syllable (vowel-balance conditions); four degrees distinguished: hauptton, starker nebenton, schwacher nebenton, unton.
new_statements.exceptions: Prefixed words with be-, of- 'too', æm-, most for- (not for- 'fore-'), many and-, mis-, o-/u- 'un-', unt-, and particle compounds (a, af, at, bort, fram, in, til, um, up, ut, væl + verb) stress the second member; many compounds (bruþlöp, husfrøa, likame, nabo, names like Gøtstaver) had fluctuating stress; loans in -era/-inna/-issa penult-stressed, -eri/-ær final-stressed; -ing/-ung derivatives alternately suffix-stressed; isolated words (væþur, mænniskia, fiande, aldrigh) and loans (bisman, kapelan, pilagrimber) with non-root stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level expiratory stress of Old Swedish as reconstructed from metre, modern pronunciation and sound laws; the grammar's declared scope (§1 language area = Sweden incl. Gotland; title 'mit Einschluss des Altgutnischen') covers Old Gutnish, and §9's list of Old Gutnish peculiarities names no accentual difference, but §57's examples are mainland Old Swedish forms — the statement applies to Old Gutnish by inclusion, not by Gutnish-specific evidence. Noreen 1913 §54 (p. 90) states explicitly that these stress conditions held 'über den ganzen Norden so ziemlich dieselben'.
new_statements.identity_note: gutn1238 'Archaic Gutnish' = Old Gutnish (Altgutnisch/forngutniska), the medieval language of Guta lag/Guta saga (Cod. Holm. B 64, c. 1350) and the Gotlandic runic inscriptions. The quoted statement (Noreen 1904 §57) is framed for Old Swedish (olds1252-type 'aschw.') whose declared scope includes Old Gutnish ('mit Einschluss des Altgutnischen'; §1 language area includes Gotland; §9 lists no accentual peculiarity of agutn.); examples are mainland Old Swedish. Noreen 1913 §54 generalises the same rule to all Old Nordic languages. Not to be confused with modern Gutnish/Gutamål (Gotland dialect of Swedish), which has modern Swedish-type tonal word accents.

tone_statements.citation: Klintberg, Mathias. 1885. Laumålets kvantitet ock aksent. (Nyare bidrag till kännedom om de svenska landsmålen ock svenskt folklif VI.1; 23:e häftet, 1885 D.) Stockholm: P. A. Norstedt & Söner. 96 pp. (pp. 1-61 = Akademisk afhandling, Uppsala, 13 Dec. 1884, 62 pp.)
tone_statements.quote: Den musikaliska aksenten är likaledes dels enkel, dels sammansatt (se NOREEN, Fårömålets ljudlära § 9). Den enkla aksenten (då stafvelsen under hela uttalstiden behåller samma tonhöjd) kommer att betecknas på följande sätt: [...] hög gravis [...] akut. Den sammansatta aksenten (då stafvelsen under uttalet vexlar tonhöjd) är dels fallande: [...] fallande cirkumflex (akut + hög gravis eller gravis, ock hög gravis + gravis) ders [sic = dels] stigande: [...] stigande cirkumflex (hög gravis + akut).
tone_statements.translation: The musical accent is likewise partly simple, partly compound (see Noreen, Fårömålets ljudlära § 9). The simple accent (when the syllable keeps the same pitch throughout its articulation) will be marked as follows: [...] high grave [...] acute. The compound accent (when the syllable changes pitch during its articulation) is partly falling: [...] falling circumflex (acute + high grave or grave, and high grave + grave), partly rising: [...] rising circumflex (high grave + acute).

tone_statements.citation: Noreen, Adolf. 1879 [issued 1881]. Fårömålets ljudlära, med ledning af C. Säves ock P. A. Säves ordsamlingar utarbetad. (Nyare bidrag till kännedom om de svenska landsmålen ock svenskt folklif I.8.) Stockholm. pp. 283-369 (sep. pag. 1-87); Tillägg ock rättelser in Sv. landsm. I.13, pp. 736-739.
tone_statements.quote: § 9. Den musikaliska aksenten är äfvenledes antingen enkel eller sammansatt. Den enkla aksenten, då stafvelsen under hela uttalstiden behåller samma tonhöjd, är af tre slag: Gravis [...] anger den lägsta tonhöjd, af hvilken man i normalt tal begagnar sig. Hög gravis [...] ligger en sekund öfver gravis. Akut [...] ligger en ters öfver gravis. [...] Den sammansatta aksenten, då stafvelsen under uttalandet växlar tonhöjd, tillkommer endast de stafvelser, som hafva sammansatt exspiratorisk aksent, ock är i målet tvåfaldig: Stigande cirkumflex [...] är sammansatt af hög gravis ock akut. [...] Fallande ci r kam fl ex [sic] [...] är sammansatt af akut ock gravis.
tone_statements.translation: § 9. The musical accent is likewise either simple or compound. The simple accent, when the syllable keeps the same pitch for its whole duration, is of three kinds: grave [...] marks the lowest pitch one uses in normal speech; high grave [...] lies a second above grave; acute [...] lies a third above grave. [...] The compound accent, when the syllable changes pitch during articulation, belongs only to those syllables that have compound expiratory accent, and is twofold in the dialect: rising circumflex [...] is composed of high grave and acute. [...] Falling circumflex [...] is composed of acute and grave.
tone_statements.locator: Sv. landsm. I.8, § 9, pp. 297-298 (sep. pag. 15-16), 'A. Ljudfysiologisk öfversikt, III. Stafvelsen' (accent-mark symbols and examples elided); rules in § 154 pp. 361-362

The 'one-peaked' characterisation in the same paragraph is cited to Pamp 1978 pp. 76-79, not to Bruce. Book not opened (print; Libris 11310840). An English-language edition of Bruce's prosody textbook appeared in 2026 (The melody and rhythm of speech: General and Swedish prosody, Manchester UP, doi 10.7765/9789198740479; coverage of Gotland and OA status not verified here).

sources.note: Per sv.wikipedia 'Gutamål' citing pp. 76-79: the word accent of gutamål is one-peaked ('entoppig'), unlike the Svealand and northern Götaland dialects where accent 2 is two-peaked. Not opened.
